system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter, checked against the Buyer Negotiation Playbook

---

## Overview

The Seller calls this a "fair and balanced package." It is neither. Almost every limitation position falls below our playbook, often at or past our fallback. Several positions combine to empty our protection further than any single clause suggests:

- Data-room deemed disclosure.
- A blanket buyer-knowledge bar.
- A clause applying the general limitations to all Claims.
- No fraud carve-out.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts several statements in its Update. The Update says Bluefen is "addressed," but the Letter confirms there is no consent and no evidence of conditions. The Update says Riverlark will be "addressed," but the Letter confirms it is unpaid with no discharge. We should use the Letter against the Update.

**No fallback authority exists.** The Seller has asked for exactly our 20% cap and 18-month fallbacks. We hold no written authority from Amelia Frost for either. We must not concede them in this round, or signal that we might.

---

## Part A: Liability regime

### 1. General cap (cl 12.1): Seller asks for 20% / AUD 4,800,000. Our position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- The Seller's figure is our conditional fallback. Using it requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft, and none has been given.
- **Push back:** re-table 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not hint at movement.
- **Escalate internally:** if the team thinks 20% may be needed later, seek Amelia Frost's written authority first, tied to this specific draft. Do not offer it as a trade before then.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2): Seller asks for AUD 25,000 de minimis and an AUD 250,000 basket recoverable on the excess only. Our position is AUD 5,000 and AUD 50,000, with first-dollar recovery.
- The de minimis is 5x ours and the basket is 5x ours.
- "Excess only" turns the basket into a deductible. We would absorb the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss permanently.
- A high de minimis also screens out small but recurring claims before they count toward the basket.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 as a tipping basket (first dollar once exceeded). Claims below the de minimis that relate to the same or similar facts should aggregate.

### 3. Time limits and the "all Claims" override (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **18 months against our 24:** this is again our fallback, and we have no Amelia Frost approval. Re-table 24 months.
- **"Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise":** this is a hidden general-regime override and the more dangerous drafting point. It would pull Title, capacity, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations (price, debt repayment, bonus funding) and covenants under the general cap, basket and 18-month period, unless we exclude each one expressly.
- **Push back:** delete it. Reverse the default so the general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Keep Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant categories in separate regimes.

### 4. Fundamental and Title warranties: Seller wants the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- Reject this. Administrative simplicity does not justify capping title at 20% of the price. If title fails, we lose the whole AUD 24,000,000 asset.
- **Push back:** a separate regime with:
  - a 100% cap;
  - at least six years;
  - no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5): these apply to "all Claims of any nature," with no fraud carve-out.
- As drafted, these would purport to cap, time-bar and exclude claims for the Seller's own fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. They would also stop us relying on pre-contract representations that were knowingly false.
- Courts may limit how far a party can contract out of its own fraud. We should not leave the outcome to litigation.
- **Push back:** insert an express carve-out, to the maximum extent enforceable, removing fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from:
  - all caps, baskets and de minimis;
  - all time limits;
  - the exclusive-remedy clause;
  - the non-reliance clause.
- This point is non-negotiable. No one on our side may waive it.

---

## Part B: Disclosure and knowledge

### 6. General disclosure (Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2])
- Paragraph [1.1] discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained **or referred to**" in the data room. The words "referred to" reach documents we may never have been given.
- Paragraph [1.2] adds the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- Together these would qualify every warranty by everything we could, in theory, have found.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete [1.1] and [1.2].
  - Disclosure should count only where it is specific, against a stated warranty, and gives enough detail for a buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - Reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or results of a prudent search.
  - The data room index can be listed as "provided," without operating as disclosure.

### 7. Paragraph [1.4] (non-admission)
- A standard non-admission clause is acceptable in principle.
- The SPA must make clear that [1.4] cannot be used to argue that a disclosed matter is not a breach, or to weaken the conditions and specific protections we negotiate on Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006.

### 8. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- The clause bars claims for anything known to the Buyer **or its advisers**, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." That is both actual and constructive knowledge, and it doubles up on the data-room disclosure.
- Here the Disclosure Letter itself tells us about Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006. Under cl 8.3, the Seller could argue we have no claim on exactly the known risks we are pricing and protecting against.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete cl 8.3.
  - If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should apply only to Seller-side warranty qualifiers, refer to named Seller knowledge persons, and require reasonable enquiry.
  - It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

---

## Part C: Deal-specific issues

### 9. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- DD-002 shows Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. Its clause 11.2 is a change-of-control clause, with conditions in 11.3.
- The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied once Bluefen's written consent is delivered. Disclosure Letter §2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the conditions are met.
- A bare consent letter may still leave the 11.3 conditions open, so the contract could fall away or be renegotiated after we have paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent to Completion, waivable by the Buyer only.
  - The condition should require an effective, unconditional consent (or one whose conditions are all satisfied), plus documentary evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer of this size.
  - Add a long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

### 10. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- About AUD 3.2m is outstanding (DD-003, change of control at 8.1, discharge at 9.2). The Seller proposes a release "following Completion."
- Disclosure Letter §3 confirms the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge.
- This conflicts with the debt-free basis. If the release comes after Completion, we take the company still encumbered and carry the risk that the Seller does not perform.
- **Push back:** require all of the following at Completion:
  - a current payout letter;
  - repayment directly from Completion funds to Riverlark;
  - executed, effective releases of all security, including PPSR registrations.
- A post-Completion release could be considered only with an irrevocable undertaking from the Seller **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither exists, so do not offer it.

### 11. DD-005 employee bonuses (funds flow)
- The Seller says the AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and leaves them out of the funds flow.
- If the Company pays them after Completion, the cost falls on us. Disclosure Letter §5 also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs are triggered.
- **Push back:**
  - The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs must either appear as a specific funds-flow line item (deducted from the price or treated as Debt) or be funded by the Seller, backed by an indemnity.
  - The Seller should confirm the on-cost position. We should not estimate an on-cost figure until that confirmation arrives.

### 12. Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- The current indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment.
- The real risk is wider. Under DD-004 clause 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- The AUD 180,000 shown as open in DD-010 is not verified independently. We should not assume it is either owed or paid.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover failure of ownership or assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party IP claims, and replacement or re-development costs.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment by the Seller (or from Completion funds) and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Request bank evidence of payment status.

### 13. DD-006 export and privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- The Seller calls this "not expected to be material." Its own Letter (§6) says the scope, any access and any notification duty are all unknown, and the export may contain about 1,240 records.
- We should not accept the Seller's "not material" label. We should also not assert that there was a confirmed breach, harm or notification duty, or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation, and give regular written updates and access before Completion.
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - The general disclosure in §6 must not operate to exclude the relevant privacy and data warranties.
  - Keep open whether a specific protection is needed once the investigation concludes.

### 14. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- The Seller says these are ordinary-course costs. Its own Letter (§8) says it is not stated whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course, and it asks that DD-008 and DD-011 be read together for timing and scope.
- **Position:** assess before deciding. We do not automatically treat this as Debt or seek a price cut.
- **Request:** the contracts, the commercial rationale, termination rights, accrual treatment, and why there are three linked AUD 110,000 renewals. Also ask whether any of this falls under the interim-period conduct covenants.

### 15. Tax and IP
- The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. They remain open.
- **Position:** reserve both and keep them as separate categories outside the general regime. We are not claiming unlimited liability, and we should not treat either as resolved.

### 16. Title evidence
- The DD-012 register is the Company's own internal record. Disclosure Letter §10 itself says it does not reflect any verification by the Buyer.
- **Request independent evidence:**
  - a current ASIC company extract;
  - share certificates;
  - allotment and transfer history;
  - the constitution, checked for pre-emption or transfer restrictions;
  - PPSR and encumbrance searches over the shares;
  - the Seller's board approvals and evidence of its capacity.
- Back all of this with the separate fundamental warranty regime in item 4.

### 17. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- These are not playbook items. The Letter characterises them as a notification obligation and an assignment restriction that is not triggered by a share sale.
- **Action:**
  - Have our counsel verify both readings independently.
  - Require the lease notification to be given at Completion.
  - Do not let [1.4] or the general disclosures stand in for confirming the position.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** No fallback authority, so do not concede. |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** No approval for 18. |
| 3 | "All Claims" limitation clause | Applies by default | **Delete.** Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, indemnities, payments and covenants. |
| 4 | Title / capacity | General cap and time limits | **100% cap, at least 6 years,** outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar |
| 5 | Fraud | No carve-out | **Express carve-out from everything.** Non-waivable. |
| 6 | Disclosure | Data room plus public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, constructive | **Delete,** or limit to named Seller persons with reasonable enquiry, with exclusions |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | **CP: effective consent plus evidence that 11.3 conditions are satisfied** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or Seller-funded, including on-costs** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden.** Keep the SOW3 cure. Verify the AUD 180k. |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve evidence, investigate, give updates.** No assumed breach and no numbers. |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first.** No automatic Debt treatment or deduction. |
| 15 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open.** Separate categories. |
| 16 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence** (ASIC, certificates, PPSR, authority) |

## Internal actions

1. **Fallback authority:** do not concede the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Seek Amelia Frost's written authority, tied to this draft, only if the team wants those fallbacks available later.
2. **Information requests to the Seller:**
   - Bluefen consent and evidence on the 11.3 conditions;
   - Riverlark payout letter;
   - bonus on-cost confirmation;
   - Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory assignment;
   - DD-006 investigation material;
   - Sandbar contracts;
   - title documents.
3. **Mark-up approach:** respond with a full mark-up, not a list of issues. This gives the Seller less room to recast our points.
=== END ADVICE ===
